newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH GOLD BOURSE VOLUME RISES ON FIRMER DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH GOLD BOURSE VOLUME RISES ON FIRMER DEMAND.

text.p: Traded volume on the Istanbul gold exchange rose to 1,645 kilos on Tuesday from Monday's 1,135 as physical demand from the free market was lifted by easier prices, dealers said.
"There was a certain rise in demand from the free market, followed by purchases in the second session due to a loosening in the ounce price," a bank dealer said.
Gold closed weaker at $327.50 an ounce and 1,725,400 lira per gram, down from $328.00 and 1,733,600 lira at Monday's close.
Dealers said seasonal activity which usually peaks in August was not as strong as expected.
The Turkish lira eased to 163,800 to the dollar from Monday's 163,350 close in line with the higher dollar/mark parity.
Most of the day's trade -- 1,160 kg -- was in the morning session and 62.3 percent of the total was conducted in lira terms.
